questions.q: Where is a Subflow actually stored on the platform, compared to a top-level Flow?
options: In a completely separate table with its own canvas language and action palette
In the exact same table as a Flow, `sys_hub_flow`, with a type flag marking it as a subflow
Only inside the legacy Workflow Editor's `wf_workflow` table
In a scoped application table that regular flows cannot access
questions.explain: A Subflow is a `sys_hub_flow` record like any Flow, flagged as a subflow type — it reuses the same triggers, actions, If/Else, and For Each building blocks.

questions.q: What is the one real test this lesson gives for deciding whether to build a Subflow instead of a top-level Flow?
options: Whether the automation is complicated enough to look impressive
Whether the logic needs to run directly off a record event or schedule, versus needing to run from inside other automation you're already building
Whether the instance has more than ten flows already
Whether the logic involves an If/Else condition
questions.explain: A Flow needs a Trigger because it reacts directly to an event or schedule; a Subflow has no trigger of its own and exists to be called from other flows that need the same logic.

questions.q: In the onboarding/offboarding/equipment-request example, what real problem does duplicating the manager-notify-and-log logic across all three flows create?
options: The flows run slower because of the duplication
ServiceNow blocks you from saving more than one flow with similar steps
A fix to that logic has to be found and applied in three separate places, and it's easy to update two and forget the third
The duplicated logic cannot use data pills
questions.explain: Copy-pasted logic across multiple flows means every future fix must be repeated in every copy — the classic failure mode a subflow eliminates by keeping the logic in one place.

questions.q: What does a Subflow NOT have, that a top-level Flow does?
options: A Trigger — a subflow only runs when called by another flow or subflow, never on its own
Any If/Else branching capability
Access to the For Each loop
The ability to use actions at all
questions.explain: Subflows share the same action and logic building blocks as flows; the structural difference is that a subflow has no Trigger and never starts on its own.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is wrapping every piece of flow logic in a subflow automatically the 'more correct' approach?
options: Yes, subflows should always be used instead of inline logic regardless of reuse
No — if logic is triggered by one specific event and nothing else needs that same sequence, a top-level Flow is still correct, and a subflow adds indirection without benefit
Yes, because subflows run faster than inline flow logic
No, because subflows cannot contain If/Else conditions
questions.explain: Subflows earn their place through actual or clearly anticipated reuse. Without that reuse, wrapping single-use logic in a subflow just adds a layer of indirection for no real benefit.
